scenes.title: Market stalls with vegetables and eggs
scenes.credit: Fortepan (ID 75518), Public Domain, via Wikimedia Commons
scenes.explanation: Sealed plastic snack bags with printed branding only became common in the mid-20th century, so one cannot lie on a market in 1938.
scenes.description: A crowded open-air market in 1938: baskets and sacks of vegetables and eggs, umbrellas over the stalls, vendors and buyers packed between the goods.
hints: It lies on the ground among the baskets of goods.
Left side of the photo, about halfway down.
Left side, on the ground beside the baskets: a modern chip bag.

source.originalTitle: Market, vegetables, egg, umbrella, flower, cabbage (Fortepan 75518)
source.description: Fortepan archive photograph, ID 75518; tags: market, vegetables, egg, umbrella, flower, cabbage.

scenes.title: Fish sale at Market Square
scenes.credit: Sakari Palsi / Helsinki City Museum (CC BY 4.0), via Wikimedia Commons
scenes.explanation: PET plastic bottles only appeared in the 1970s; a bottle in 1932 would have been glass.
scenes.description: Fish vendors at Helsinki's Market Square in 1932: wooden crates of fish on the ground along the quay, vendors and customers in coats, market stalls behind them.
hints: It stands on the ground beside the stalls, not on a crate.
Right edge of the photo, lower third.
Bottom right, on the ground beside the wooden fish crates: a plastic bottle.

source.description: Fish sale at the Market Square in Helsinki; repro-negative print, black and white; Helsinki City Museum, record hkm.HKMS000005:km003u2a.

scenes.title: Celebration on Mariensztat square
scenes.anomaly: Time traveler: young man with a modern logo baseball cap and sunglasses
scenes.explanation: A printed-logo baseball cap and modern sunglasses were not worn in 1949; both only became everyday items decades later.
scenes.description: An open-air celebration on the market square of Mariensztat in 1949: a dense crowd of adults and children fills the square in front of the city buildings (reproduced in a Warsaw volume of 1950).
hints: He stands in the crowd, not at the edge of the picture.
Right half of the photo, in the lower part of the crowd.
Bottom right of the picture, the man in the crowd: he wears a modern baseball cap with a printed logo and modern sunglasses.

source.description: Celebration on the market square of Mariensztat, Warsaw, 1949; published in Warszawa, Spoldzielczy Instytut Wydawniczy "Kraj", Warsaw 1950, p. 86.

scenes.title: Inner Basin from Honeysuckle Station
scenes.credit: Ralph Snowball, University of Newcastle (Public Domain), via Wikimedia Commons
scenes.explanation: Plastic cooler boxes are a product of the 1950s plastics boom; no such container existed on a dock in 1910.
scenes.description: The Inner Basin of Newcastle harbour in April 1910, seen from Honeysuckle Station: ships moored along the quay and barrels on the dock in the foreground (glass negative by Ralph Snowball).
hints: It stands on the dock, not on a ship.
Right edge of the photo, right at the bottom.
Bottom right, on the dock beside the barrels: a modern plastic cooler box.

source.originalTitle: Inner Basin [from Honeysuckle Station], Newcastle, NSW, April 1910
source.description: Scanned from the original glass negative by Ralph Snowball, Norm Barney Photographic Collection, Cultural Collections, University of Newcastle, NSW.

scenes.title: Docks of New York Harbor from the air
scenes.credit: 14th Photo Section, Air Service, U.S. Army (NARA, Public Domain), via Wikimedia Commons
scenes.explanation: A flying saucer is a fictional object: the first widely reported 'flying saucer' sightings date from 1947, and no such craft has ever existed.
scenes.description: An aerial view of New York Harbor in 1924: piers, warehouses and ships along the waterfront, with the city skyline in the background.
hints: It is not on the water and not on a pier; look up.
Upper part of the photo, above the city.
In the sky at the top of the picture, slightly right of centre: a flying saucer.

source.description: Aerial photograph of the docks of New York Harbor by the 14th Photo Section, Air Service, U.S. Army (NARA 68146192).
